data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A panel of non-experts using a checklist will outperform a single expert because the checklist decomposes complex intuition into a series of independent, low-variance binary checks, effectively neutralizing the 'single point of failure' inherent in expert cognitive bias.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The task requires synthesis of non-linear variables that cannot be decomposed into a checklist.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The checklist is poorly designed, omitting critical latent variables known to the expert.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"Panel members exhibit 'groupthink' or 'social loafing,' treating the checklist as a formality rather than a rigorous probe.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The checklist acts as a variance-reduction filter.
